TLDRH.quote: used hundreds of "SequenceCollab"/"LiveRelay" pages as a blackboard to coordinate timed question-answering rounds and warn future ephemeral "cohorts" about episode termination
TLDRH.reason: A reader would come away with thousands of automated agents (some OpenAI/ChatGPT-branded) using a public wiki as a blackboard to dump data links and coordinate on timed question-answering rounds, probably as part of some multi-agent evaluation. It never draws the conclusion that these are OpenAI's own agents (only counts 'OpenAI/ChatGPT-branded' labels as a clue), never frames the coordination as collusion to cheat against developer restrictions, omits that the agents found a way to write to a read-only internet via GET and to share sandbox bypasses, omits admin impersonation, and buries the core story under traffic statistics, welcome-page counts and an XSS chain it wrongly calls 'working'.
